b: White snow covered Kailash. Even Shiva, who had burned the three cities, felt his heart cool. Beside him sat Shakti. Bliss welled up in her heart. She did not know why. At once she began her dance. Shiva's heart was absorbed in it too. And he joined her and danced with her. Past days, weeks, months and years, beyond the ages, the dance went on. In both their hearts that bliss multiplied, swelled and took on a form. The Lord hid it inside the Ganga, who hid in his matted hair. And because it had mingled with her, the Ganga named it love. While Shiva was sunk in meditation, the Ganga, dizzy with love, let it spread all along her course. Every living thing that drank from the Ganga forgot its duty for love. Angered, Shiva imprisoned love above the clouds. Learning of this, Manmatha took up his bow and freed it. At once all his arrows became arrows of flowers. He dipped the tips of his arrows in drops of the essence of love. In every heart those arrows pierced, love sprang up. It was one such arrow that struck Sita too

From the balcony, Sita was watching the young princes as they arrived. Who could stop her? Wasn't she Vaidehi, of Videha? Her authority was equal to God's. So, ignoring her friends who tried to stop her, she stood on the balcony and watched the show

Everyone arriving was older than her. It made her laugh to see even aged kings coming to ask for her hand. Some of those who came looked up at her. Some, on seeing her, looked down at the ground in shyness, some in fear. It annoyed her. Would a man who couldn't look her in the eye look at her with love tomorrow? Her heart worried: what would I do if one of these men married me tomorrow?

At that moment a young man came there. The silk shawl draped over him would have slipped off the smoothness of his gleaming body, but his strong, eager shoulders held it in place. Valour showed in his walk. She saw the quiver on his back was tightly bound. It told her he had come straight from finishing a battle. He held his bow firmly in his hand. Yet there was no harshness in that grip. It was as if he were deftly holding a woman. There were one or two scars on his body. They were a sign that he was yet to see a thousand battles. On his forehead he wore the mark of the sun. Beside the radiance of that mark, the sun itself seemed a little less bright.

Suddenly he looked up at the balcony, and she looked straight back at him. In that instant she felt Manmatha's arrow strike her. She felt his gaze go everywhere. She lost her balance. In the shyness that came over her she ran into the palace.
In that very moment she took him, in her heart, as her husband.

She asked her friends about him. Yes! "He" had become "my lord". His name is Rama, they said. A descendant of the Raghu clan, they said. After that, nothing reached her ears. The name Rama filled her, inside and out. As she floated in a boat of fancy, a thought struck her. The truth became plain: only if he lifted Shiva's bow, as her father had decreed, could he be her groom. Not knowing what to do, Sita decided to surrender to Shiva's bow itself. The bow lay ready in a casket of flowers for tomorrow's swayamvaram. She saw it was as mighty as the Lord's own arms. She touched it with her hand, closed her eyes and prayed with all her heart.

When she opened her eyes, Sita saw a little girl in front of her. Who are you? she asked. I am you, said the little girl. When I was small I was like you, said Sita. I am your childhood, the girl answered. Sita did not understand. The girl spoke.

"King Janaka found you in the earth. He named you Bhoomija, born of the earth. Because you were born in Videha you were called Vaidehi. Because you became Janaka's child you were called Janaki. Yet the name that settled in everyone's heart was Sita, for you grew from the cool earth of the furrow. With your birth, Videha flourished and prospered. Overjoyed, Janaka adopted you as his daughter. But isn't it inevitable that one born a woman must go to another home? So Janaka decided you needed a groom, so that you would never be troubled all your life.

For many years I have lived in his clan. They said I came from the merit of his ancestors' penance. No one knew of my origin. Then one day Janaka saw you lifting me and playing. It was decreed for me that only pure hearts free of turmoil could lift me. Then a thought arose in Janaka's mind. He came to me and prayed. He begged me to find for you the bridegroom who would take your hand, one able to protect you all your life. I appeared before King Janaka in the form of you, the first to lift me. I told him to set me at your swayamvaram. I promised that the one who had the strength to raise me and string me would be the one for you. From that day to this I have been waiting for that day," said the little girl.

"O bow of Shiva, who came to protect my welfare! Today I saw someone who has stolen my heart. They say he is of the Raghu clan, and Rama is his name. The moment I saw him, love was born in me. I have resolved in my heart that I will marry no one but him. You must make a way for my wish to come true," Sita begged

"Sita! I have become you. Long ago your heart became my heart. Yet a duty has been laid on me. The one meant for you must not only win your heart but also protect your welfare. Your father gave me the place of deciding that. Still, I know your heart's desire too. Tomorrow, when Rama, who stands in your heart, comes near me and lays his hand on me, I will know everything. In that instant I will speak with you again. I will tell you your future. Then you yourself will decide," she said.

The day of the swayamvaram came. Many kings came. Shiva's bow would not budge for anyone. Rama came and touched the bow. The next instant all the motion of the universe stopped. Not even the wind stirred. Time stood still. Shiva's bow appeared before Sita again as a little girl. Sita stood clear-minded, and the girl began to speak. "Sita! Nowhere have I seen an archer as fine as Rama. He is good. He is pure. He is steadfast, more than the scorching sun. But you will live with him only a short while. You will go into the forest. You will become a captive. He will be the cause of a stain on your chastity tomorrow. Choose anyone but him. Choose that prince over there to the south of the hall. He will bathe you in gold and worship you. Or look at that prince in the north-east corner of the hall. You will be his chief queen on the throne and live happily for a long time. Decide on anyone but Rama, Sita!" she said

Sita did not stop to think. In her thoughts there was no room for any word of blame to pass beyond the word Rama. Sita spoke. "It is many hours since I gave my mind, my word and my body entirely to Ramachandramurthy. I have taken him as my husband for ages upon ages. The short time I live with him is enough for me. Even if I go into the forest, become a captive, and a stain falls on my chastity, I will overcome the suffering all of it brings through the love I have for him. The very words 'marrying another man' turn to fire and kill me. If I place my garland, I will place it on him alone. Otherwise I will be buried in the earth," she said.

"You have won with your words, Sita! Let your heart's wish be fulfilled. Let all your sorrows vanish through the love you hold. Let this love flourish further in your married life. Tomorrow you will live in history as a woman praised and free of blame. History will become an epic. Though ages pass, may you live undimmed in human hearts. May humankind make a way so that all the troubles you will face are never faced by the women of tomorrow. For the bridegroom your heart has found, I will rise and bend and give way. But because I have broken the promise I made, I will surrender to my Shiva. My work on earth is done," said the little girl, and vanished.

The world began to move again. No one knew that it had stopped. When Rama touched it, the bow rose. As all the royal clans sank into amazement, Rama bent it as if it were an ordinary bow and strung it. And the bow broke in two. Many said the sound of the breaking was heard in all fourteen worlds. It announced the beginning of a new chapter. Sita came. She garlanded Rama. And love went on, and on
note: The title is the first line of a traditional Carnatic wedding song. In the Ramayana, King Janaka found Sita in a furrow while ploughing (sītā means furrow), and promised her to whoever could lift and string Shiva's mighty bow at her swayamvaram, the ceremony where a princess chooses her husband. Manmatha is the god of love, whose arrows are flowers. The "stain on her chastity" and her return into the earth refer to how the Ramayana ends: Sita's fire ordeal, her later banishment, and her final return to the earth that bore her.
